summary: Willamette NF lookout: first cab c.1930-33, burned 1968, cab moved from Whisky Peak and rebuilt 1989, NHLR 1990; staffed in summer, gated spur road.

facts.design: Grange-hall-style gable-roofed L-4 cab (14 x 14 gable-roof house c.1931 per Forest Lookouts); the current cab came from Whisky Peak and was set on a 10-foot treated timber tower in 1989

staffing.status: staffed during the summer field season; NHLR says it doubles as a lookout in high fire season and an interpretive center
staffing.as_of: undated Society page; its road note says as of 2025

access.note: Spur road gated 1.25 miles from the lookout; Old Santiam Wagon Road (FS #810) in poor condition, high clearance recommended. NHLR lists the lookout as available for rental.

visit.trail_note: Spur road to the lookout is gated 1.25 miles from it; season runs late June to mid October

events.note: July 1926 newspaper: an additional lookout would be stationed on Sand Mountain if the fire hazard stayed high
firelookout.com: established 1932 with a gable-roofed L-4 cab. Forest Lookouts says c.1931; the Society gives 1930 as the style date and 1933 for the Grange-hall-style L-4
Big Lake fire, August 1967, swept over the summit; the station survived it
Burned to the ground per a Eugene Register-Guard report dated July 1, 1968; Forest Service said the cause was unknown; firelookout.com says it accidentally burned
Pop-up cupola trailer used as a temporary lookout from 1968
Cab moved from Whisky Peak and rebuilt; a 10-foot treated timber tower was erected for it
Dedication ceremony for the new lookout in 1990
National Historic Lookout Register registration date August 18, 1990

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Build year varies. firelookout.com says 1932 for a gable-roofed L-4 cab, Forest Lookouts says a 14 x 14 gable-roof house around 1931, and the Society gives 1930 as the style date and 1933 for the Grange-hall-style L-4. The record keeps 1932 and the story gives the range.

The Forest Service said the cause of the 1968 fire was unknown, while firelookout.com says the cab accidentally burned. The story reports the Forest Service wording and notes the firelookout.com claim.

NHLR calls the 1980s effort a complete restoration of the early building. The Society says the cab was moved from Whisky Peak and rebuilt in 1989. Both are cited, and the story describes the move and rebuild.
NHLR gives 5,366 ft (1,636 m), the Society gives 5,460 ft (1,664 m) and firelookout.com gives 5459 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure of 1635.6 m.

notes_for_editor: The 1968 burning is consistent across sources; the build year (1930 to 1933) is contested and the record's 1932 is only firelookout.com's date. The only dated item is the Society page's 'As of 2025' road note, so the staffing as_of is that page's undated wording. Rental is listed by NHLR only; confirm with the Society before publishing rental details. Access level restricted because the spur road is gated 1.25 miles away. Not visited.
